For teaching: a per-student or per-exercise 'system prompt' — base conventions plus conditionally injected hints, scaffolding level, and error-message verbosity — is a more scalable way to differentiate instruction than writing N separate lesson variants.

If you adopt conditional prompt/module assembly without a way to inspect what was actually assembled for a given run, you lose debuggability — the same trap as opaque build systems.
